notes: No rack mounting (portable beltpack, worn on belt clip; 46 x 95 x 119 mm, 261 g). Device has exactly two physical connectors: 1x Neutrik EtherCON (RJ45-compatible) for combined data+PoE power, and 1x Neutrik XLR4-M for headset (mic in + audio out combined). Network grade confirmed as 10/100 Mbps (Fast Ethernet, eth-100m) explicitly per manufacturer manual - this is NOT gigabit. No separate AC/DC power inlet exists; power arrives exclusively via PoE on the EtherCON port. The XLR4 headset jack is technically a signal connector (mic+audio), but the provided connector enum's only 4-pin-XLR option is "xlr4-dc" (DC-power-flavored) - selected as closest id per instructions, flagged here since it is not actually a DC power port. Cross-checked against manufacturer product page (greengocom.com/products/bpx) and UK retailer Canford listing ("ethercon RJ45"), both consistent.

ports.name: Network/PoE
ports.note: Neutrik EtherCON (RJ45-based); serves as both data network connection and sole power input via PoE (IEEE 802.3af, 48-56 Vdc)

ports.name: Headset
ports.note: Neutrik XLR4-Male headset connector combining mic input (pins 1&2, unbalanced, up to 2.5V bias, +30 to +60 dB gain) and headset audio output (pins 3&4, 0 dBu nominal / +20 dBu max, 120 ohm output driving 32-600 ohm headsets). The permitted connector list has no generic signal XLR4 id; xlr4-dc (normally DC-power-coded) is the closest available match for a 4-pin XLR - it is NOT used for DC power on this device.
